main_text.p: ut in singulis explicabitur. Istam distinctionem tradunt Talmudici in libro שבועות fol.16.2. & Megilla fol.22.2. Partic. pahul, ברוך Benedictus, Laudatus: Fœmininum, ברוכה Benedicta,Ruth.3.10. Infin. לברך Ad benedicendum ei, 1.Sam.13.v.10. Futur. ינברכו Flectamus genua, Psalm.95.6. ויברך Et flexit genua,2.Paralip.6.13. Chald. Particip. praesens, ברך Procumbens in genua, Daniel.6.10. Particip. Pehil בריך Benedictus, Dan.3.v.28. Niph.Praeterit. ונברכו בך Et benedicta erunt in te, Genes.12.3. & 18.v.18. Pih. ברך Benedixit: Salutavit, Valedixit, in accessu vel recessu usurpatum. Per euphemiam est etiam quandoq, Maledixit. Construitur cum Accusat. Praeteritum, ברך את ארני Benedixit Domino meo,Genes.24.35. pro Maledixit, 1.Reg.21.10.13. Job.1.5.11. Futurum, וכי יברכך איש Et si salutaverit te aliquis, 2. Reg.4.29. ויברכו את רבקה Et valedixerunt Rebecca, Genes.24.60. Chald. Praeter. ברך Benedixit, Dan.2.19. ברכת Benedixi, Daniel.4.13. Pyh. Futur. יברך Benedicetur, Prov.22.9. תברך Idem, Prov.20.v.21. Part. מברך Benedictum, Psalm.113.2. Chald. Particip. מברך Benedictum,Dan.2.10. Hiph.Infinit. אברך Ingeniculandum, Genua flectenda esse, Genes.41. verf.43. cum א loco characteristici ה , ut Jerem.25.v.3. Jesa.63.3. in similibus exemplis. Esse autem Infinitivum, docet Verbum continuo sequens, ונתון Et dedisse sive Constituisse; tum etiam confirmat R. Jonah, ut Aben Esra citat: Nempe regius praeco in Josephi inauguratione ante currum proclamavit, Flectenda esse genua omnibus coram Josepho; Constitutum enim eum esse supremum Praefectum totius Aegypti. Variant interpretes. Allegorici scribunt; אברך dicitur quasi אב בחכמה Pater sapientia, ורך בשנים & tener annis. Futurum, ויברך Et effecit

page.notes: Several Hebrew words are uncertain at this scan resolution: ינברכו, בריך, ונתון, אברך (Hiph.), ורך בשנים and the Hebrew in the final line. They are given as read, without [?], because the marks would be unreliable. The catchword "effecit" is partly obscured and is read from its visible shape. Long s has been normalised to s. Italic and roman boundaries in the Latin are approximate. The running head is the Hebrew entry letters בר, with no title in Latin letters.
